summary: IBM Maximo leads the cohort because it owns critical-asset workflow data, maintenance execution, and high-switching-cost enterprise operations. BrainBox AI/Trane is the strongest pure autonomous-control story. Runwise, 75F, and GridPoint are resilient because software intelligence connects to physical building systems and measurable outcomes. Accruent and Planon are resilient enterprise workflow platforms, while Facilio is promising and unusually agent-ready but still has a newer, more copyable agentic layer.

quadrant.placement: IBM Maximo and BrainBox AI/Trane lead the resilient quadrant; Runwise, 75F, GridPoint, Accruent, and Planon are also resilient; Facilio sits near the resilient boundary.
quadrant.rationale: Physical and critical workflow control raises resilience. Enterprise workflow platforms remain defensible when AI is tied to governed records and actions rather than generic assistant output.

context.rationale: Maximo manages asset history, work data, maintenance workflows, inspections, sensor data, and reliability context across critical infrastructure.

trust.rationale: IBM's enterprise cloud/security posture, Maximo security documentation, and critical-industry customer base support high trust.

distribution.rationale: IBM sells Maximo across manufacturing, energy, utilities, transportation, government, healthcare, and other asset-intensive sectors.

judgment.rationale: Maximo embeds reliability, inspection, and maintenance logic, but final operational judgment remains with asset owners and technicians.

liability_governance.rationale: The suite supports compliance, safety, inspections, work control, and governed asset records, though customer operators retain final liability.

frequency.rationale: Maintenance, inspection, reliability, and work-order processes are daily operating workflows in asset-intensive organizations.

operational_dependence.rationale: IBM positions Maximo around uptime, safety, compliance, outage reduction, and reliability for critical equipment and infrastructure.

system_position.rationale: Maximo acts as a system of record and action for assets, work orders, maintenance processes, and reliability workflows.

switching_cost.rationale: Historical asset data, integrations, work processes, training, and compliance records make migration materially costly.

budget_durability.rationale: Critical-asset uptime, safety, inspections, and regulated maintenance are durable budget lines.

model_improvement_test.rationale: IBM describes AI and sensor-data use for issue detection, prioritization, forecasting, and predictive maintenance.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: The moat is enterprise asset data, workflows, integrations, and operational governance, not a thin AI interface.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: IBM's platform and integration posture can support agentic workflows, but the public Maximo evidence is stronger for AI insights than explicit MCP-style delegation.

accountability_test.rationale: Maximo governs inspected and maintenance-controlled workflows, but accountability remains shared with operators.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: The product targets uptime, reliability, safety, asset life, production continuity, and field execution.

context.rationale: The system uses building telemetry, weather, occupancy, energy use, HVAC behavior, and control data.

trust.rationale: BrainBox cites SOC 2 Type II, encryption, RBAC/MFA, NIST alignment, and Trane's enterprise building-controls distribution.

distribution.rationale: Trane acquired BrainBox AI and routes it through a global HVAC and building-management customer base.

judgment.rationale: Autonomous control and diagnostics encode domain-specific HVAC and energy judgment, though building operators still own final business constraints.

liability_governance.rationale: Trane/BrainBox operate in safety- and comfort-sensitive controls workflows with security controls, but public evidence still leaves customer operating responsibility in place.

frequency.rationale: HVAC optimization and control run continuously, not episodically.

operational_dependence.rationale: The product affects energy cost, comfort, emissions, maintenance prioritization, and building operations.

system_position.rationale: It integrates with Trane controls and building systems, but may sit alongside existing BMS infrastructure rather than replace all control layers.

switching_cost.rationale: Building integrations, tuned control models, and operational trust create switching friction.

budget_durability.rationale: Energy reduction, carbon goals, and HVAC performance are direct budget and compliance concerns.

model_improvement_test.rationale: The value proposition is model-driven autonomous HVAC prediction, optimization, and conversational building intelligence.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: The moat is connected building control, telemetry, Trane distribution, and autonomous execution, not generic model output.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: ARIA and Trane AI-agent claims support conversational diagnosis and workflow assistance, but public evidence is less explicit on open delegated-agent APIs.

accountability_test.rationale: Trane's enterprise support and BrainBox security posture add accountability beyond recommendations.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: Claims center on energy-cost reduction, carbon reduction, comfort, and operational building performance.

context.rationale: Runwise uses wireless hardware, indoor sensors, weather forecasts, building-response history, usage data, and live operating state.

trust.rationale: Runwise claims 10,300+ powered buildings, 1,000+ customers, 24/7 support, utility relationships, and dedicated building experts.

distribution.rationale: Runwise has strong property-owner deployment in its core market, though narrower global reach than large incumbents.

judgment.rationale: The system embeds building-control logic and field-service expertise rather than just surfacing dashboards.

liability_governance.rationale: Runwise provides service accountability and savings claims, but public terms leave core safety and equipment responsibility with customers.

frequency.rationale: Heating, cooling, water, and alerting systems are continuously monitored or controlled.

operational_dependence.rationale: The product affects tenant comfort, energy cost, critical alerts, emissions/fines, and building operations.

system_position.rationale: Runwise sits in the monitoring and control layer, but does not replace every safety, equipment, or BMS function.

switching_cost.rationale: Installed devices, sensor data, integrations, service routines, and building-specific behavior models create switching friction.

budget_durability.rationale: Runwise ties budget to energy savings, rebates, carbon fines, and operating profit.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Runwise's current AI-control evidence describes decisions that skip or run heat cycles using indoor data, forecasts, seasonality, and prior response.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: The moat is installed controls, wireless sensors, operational data, service, and measured outcomes.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Runwise says it has open APIs and many integrations, but public evidence is thinner on autonomous third-party agent governance.

accountability_test.rationale: No long-term contracts, 24/7 support, dedicated experts, technician service, and savings guarantees add commercial accountability.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: The product directly targets energy savings, comfort, fines, leak/gas/heating alerts, and building operations.

context.rationale: 75F owns building telemetry from sensors, controllers, thermostats, gateways, analytics, apps, and BAS workflows.

trust.rationale: 75F publishes SOC 2 Type 1 evidence, security controls, encryption, audit logs, RBAC/MFA, and network/gateway security.

distribution.rationale: Public sources and company releases show meaningful installations and recognizable customer logos, though less scale than IBM, Trane, or GridPoint.

judgment.rationale: 75F embeds HVAC, IAQ, demand-response, and building-automation logic in hardware and software.

liability_governance.rationale: Security, audit logs, BACnet/OpenADR/Project Haystack posture, and building-control workflows support governance, though final operations remain customer-owned.

frequency.rationale: Building automation, comfort, IAQ, and HVAC controls operate continuously.

operational_dependence.rationale: The system affects comfort, HVAC energy use, IAQ, demand response, and building performance.

system_position.rationale: 75F provides full-stack BAS functions but may coexist with other building systems and integrators.

switching_cost.rationale: Installed hardware, control sequences, data integrations, and operator training create migration cost.

budget_durability.rationale: Energy efficiency, comfort, IAQ, and controls budgets are durable, but buyer economics vary by building segment.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Better models should improve control sequencing, diagnostics, IAQ optimization, and demand-response decisions over sensor/control data.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: 75F is hardware, controls, APIs, apps, and automation, not a software-only model wrapper.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Project Haystack open APIs and BACnet/OpenADR support system interoperability, though public evidence is not MCP-style agent governance.

accountability_test.rationale: Security, controls, SOC evidence, and building-automation responsibilities create accountability beyond recommendations.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: 75F targets HVAC savings, IAQ, comfort, demand response, and building automation outcomes.

context.rationale: GridPoint uses equipment-level data, meters, sensors, controls, schedules, alerts, building assets, and historical energy data.

trust.rationale: Large deployed footprint and utility/commercial energy role support trust, but public SOC/ISO security evidence was not found in sampled sources.

distribution.rationale: GridPoint says its platform is deployed across 20,000+ commercial buildings and is nearing $1.5B in customer savings.

judgment.rationale: Energy optimization, demand response, and asset-control algorithms encode operational energy judgment.

liability_governance.rationale: Demand-response reporting and IPMVP-style savings evidence support governance, but formal safety/security/legal accountability is less public.

frequency.rationale: Energy monitoring, schedules, controls, and demand response are continuous or frequent operating workflows.

operational_dependence.rationale: GridPoint affects energy cost, HVAC performance, occupant comfort, food quality, compliance readiness, and maintenance costs.

system_position.rationale: It controls and monitors building energy assets, but is more energy-focused than a full BAS or CMMS.

switching_cost.rationale: Installed controllers, energy history, utility programs, schedules, and operational reporting create switching friction.

budget_durability.rationale: Energy savings, demand response, and grid-interactive building economics are durable operating budget drivers.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Better models should improve forecasting, optimization, diagnostics, and curtailment strategy over GridPoint's building-energy data.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: Controls, metering, demand response, utility programs, and building asset data make GridPoint deeper than a dashboard wrapper.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Public evidence supports automation and controls, but not explicit AI-agent interfaces or delegated-action governance.

accountability_test.rationale: Customer savings, demand-response performance, real-time monitoring, and remote diagnostics make outcomes inspectable.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: The product targets energy cost, carbon, HVAC performance, food quality, grid services, and maintenance reduction.

context.rationale: Accruent stores and connects work orders, asset records, engineering documents, IoT signals, audit records, space data, and facilities history.

trust.rationale: Accruent publishes ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, UK ICO alignment, and critical-infrastructure compliance commitments.

distribution.rationale: Accruent says it has helped more than 10,000 organizations in more than 150 countries.

judgment.rationale: The products encode facilities, maintenance, engineering-document, and compliance workflows, while scarce judgment often remains with customers and technicians.

liability_governance.rationale: Accruent emphasizes compliance, audit logs, role controls, configurable security, and regulated workflows.

frequency.rationale: Maintenance, asset, space, document, and monitoring workflows are recurrent, though frequency varies by product and user.

operational_dependence.rationale: Accruent positions its products around downtime reduction, compliance readiness, predictive maintenance, and asset lifecycle optimization.

system_position.rationale: Products act as systems of record and action for facilities and asset workflows while coexisting with ERP, BMS, and field-service systems.

switching_cost.rationale: Configured workflows, history, integrations, training, audit records, and implementation work create migration cost.

budget_durability.rationale: Maintenance, compliance, asset uptime, and facilities-management spend are durable, but broad modules vary in budget priority.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Crue AI, predictive maintenance, Observe, EDMS automation, and analytics should improve when grounded in proprietary workflow context.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: Generic AI can copy assistant features, but cannot easily replace installed records, integrations, and governance.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Accruent has REST APIs and integrations, but public evidence is stronger for conventional integration than explicit delegated-agent control.

accountability_test.rationale: Compliance, auditability, security controls, and services give Accruent an accountability layer beyond AI output.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: The products target downtime, compliance, energy, asset life, operational continuity, and safety-adjacent work.

context.rationale: Planon unifies real estate, facilities, workplace, asset, service, energy, sustainability, and IoT-enabled building data.

trust.rationale: Planon's trust center cites independent audits, ISO 27001, ISAE 3402 Type II, SOC 2, and other assurance signals.

distribution.rationale: Planon positions itself as a global smart sustainable building management provider with broad IWMS adoption.

judgment.rationale: Embedded AI and IWMS workflows encode facilities, space, asset, contract, and maintenance judgment, but operators keep final decisions.

liability_governance.rationale: Planon emphasizes validated unified data, GDPR compliance, certifications, and governed cloud services.

frequency.rationale: Workplace, service, maintenance, and portfolio workflows are recurring, though not all modules are daily for all users.

operational_dependence.rationale: The platform supports real estate, facility management, asset maintenance, workplace services, and sustainability operations.

system_position.rationale: Planon is an IWMS/source-of-truth layer with IoT and smart-building integration, but often coexists with controls, ERP, and service systems.

switching_cost.rationale: Portfolio data, configured workflows, integrations, and service processes create migration cost.

budget_durability.rationale: Real estate, facilities, maintenance, and sustainability management are durable but can be cyclical by module.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Planon describes embedded AI for ticket creation, contract summaries, adaptive maintenance, triage, and building intelligence.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: The moat is unified validated IWMS data and workflow integration, not standalone AI text generation.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Planon has platform and integration posture, but public evidence is less explicit on external agent/MCP-style execution.

accountability_test.rationale: Trust-center controls, validated data, GDPR compliance, and governed workflows support accountability.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: Planon targets cost, utilization, maintenance, energy, workplace services, and sustainability outcomes.

context.rationale: Facilio unifies assets, work orders, tenants, vendors, compliance, finance, energy, refrigeration, and portfolio operations.

trust.rationale: Facilio states SOC 2 compliance and security controls, but its public security page also says it is working toward SOC2 compliant standards, creating some evidence ambiguity.

distribution.rationale: Facilio has visible enterprise portfolio customers and multi-site positioning, but less established reach than IBM, Accruent, Planon, or Trane.

judgment.rationale: Atom agents are designed to execute service, finance, compliance, approval, reporting, and dispatch workflows, not just record them.

liability_governance.rationale: MCP permissions, OAuth2, and audit trails are strong, but broader liability and compliance posture is less proven publicly than mature incumbents.

frequency.rationale: Service requests, work orders, vendor coordination, compliance, and invoices are recurring operational workflows.

operational_dependence.rationale: For multi-site FM teams, Facilio can become operationally important, though it may layer on top of existing CMMS/ERP systems.

system_position.rationale: Facilio can be the connected CMMS/platform layer or an AI layer over existing CMMS, ERP, and finance systems.

switching_cost.rationale: Operational workflows, integrations, agent configurations, and portfolio data create friction once deployed.

budget_durability.rationale: Facilities uptime, vendor coordination, compliance, and back-office labor reduction have durable budget logic.

model_improvement_test.rationale: Facilio's Atom and MCP posture should benefit directly from better models that can coordinate FM workflows and retrieve operational context.

wrapper_risk_test.rationale: Facilio is more than a wrapper, but its most visible differentiation is AI-agent orchestration that other platforms may copy.

agent_readiness_test.rationale: Facilio MCP connects Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Cursor to Facilio data with permissions, OAuth2, and audit logs.

accountability_test.rationale: Audit trails, permissions, human oversight, and workflow execution controls support accountability.

outcome_depth_test.rationale: The suite targets service intake, dispatch, compliance, invoice validation, reporting, maintenance, and asset lifecycle outcomes.

IBM Maximo: Expose clearer permissioned agent interfaces for work planning and execution.
Keep AI tied to governed asset records, inspections, and maintenance actions.
BrainBox AI/Trane: Make agent permissions and operator override controls visible.
Expand from HVAC optimization into broader building operations while preserving control trust.
Runwise: Publish clearer security and controls-governance evidence.
Keep extending from heating into broader building systems without losing installation speed.
75F: Refresh public AI launch evidence and adoption metrics.
Make permissioned automation and operator-override governance more explicit.
GridPoint: Clarify AI/model layer and agent-readiness claims.
Publish stronger security and controls-governance evidence.
Accruent: Make AI action-safe inside governed workflows.
Expose clearer agent-grade controls for maintenance, compliance, and asset work.
Planon: Make AI execution permissions and audit trails more visible.
Deepen integration between IWMS intelligence and building-control actions.
Facilio: Publish clearer SOC/security attestations and live-agent case outcomes.
Tie agents to durable compliance and financial controls that competitors cannot copy quickly.

final_verdict: The resilient end of this market is defined by ownership of trusted operational context, control authority, recurring work, and accountable outcomes. IBM Maximo is strongest overall; BrainBox AI/Trane is the strongest AI-control story; Runwise, 75F, and GridPoint are strong physical/energy-control platforms; Accruent and Planon are resilient workflow platforms; Facilio is agent-native but still needs more proof that agentic execution becomes durable workflow ownership.

confidence.reason: Official evidence is strong for product scope, trust posture, workflow depth, and many outcome claims. Remaining uncertainty is private retention, live implementation quality, customer-level economics, and unpublished agent/control governance.

comparison.relative_summary: The spread is partly category-driven. Critical-asset systems and physical control platforms score higher because better AI can act on proprietary operating context. IWMS/FM platforms remain defensible when AI is tied to governed records, compliance, and workflow execution.
key_differences: IBM Maximo wins on critical-asset workflow depth and switching cost.
BrainBox AI/Trane, Runwise, 75F, and GridPoint benefit from physical control or energy-control loops.
Accruent and Planon win on enterprise workflow breadth and trust/compliance posture.
Facilio wins on explicit agent readiness but has less long-term proof of durable agentic workflow ownership.
